Who this worksheet is for

This Year 9 / KS3 resource explains why expanding two brackets produces four products, using an area model before moving to negative signs, non-unit coefficients and squared brackets.

The six-page main PDF contains four lesson and exercise pages and two solution pages. The free download also includes a separate two-page Expanding and Factorising homework: one practice page and one page of worked answers. The same companion homework is included with the Factorising Quadratics resource.

6 pages + 2-page homework · Answers

What the worksheet covers

  • The four products and an area model
  • Collecting like terms
  • Keeping negative signs with their terms
  • Coefficients and squared brackets
  • Rectangle area and perimeter
  • Error spotting, independent checks and mixed follow-up homework

Prerequisites: multiplying terms, expanding a single bracket and collecting like terms. Use separate paper where more working space is needed. The companion homework's 12-15 minute target is flexible. Suggested teaching marks are not an official examination scheme; no exam board is claimed.

Key ideas at a glance

Multiply every term by every term

For (x + 3)(x + 4), the four products are x², 4x, 3x and 12. Collecting like terms gives x² + 7x + 12.

Keep the middle term when squaring

(x - 3)² means (x - 3)(x - 3). The two cross-products total -6x, so the expansion is x² - 6x + 9.
